title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - A-18
notes:
West leads the ♦J to his East's ♦A. East returns a diamond which South wins. South has already lost a trick to the ♦A and has 2 certain spade losers. South must therefore play the heart suit for no losers. South must find the ♥Q.

It is a well known fact that when holding 8 cards in a suit containing all of the honours except the Queen, one should generally finesse against that card. Many players holding the above combination would make the mistake of cashing the ♥A or ♥K before taking a second round heart finesse. This plan will fail when East has 4 hearts to the ♥Q.

The above line of play will succeed when West has a singleton ♥Q. As there are 4 small hearts and only 1 ♥Q outstanding, a singleton heart with West is four times more likely to be a small one. South can guard against this distribution by crossing to dummy and taking a first round trump finesse.

When that finesse wins, South can cross to dummy and finesse trumps again. The ♥A and ♥K will draw East's last 2 trumps. South concedes 2 spade tricks to the defense.
